findings.message: upgrade_idle() checks only scheduler.active, admission.active, admission.task and the queue's pending/active entries. It ignores TicketWriter continuations, which are tickets paused at a stage boundary (next_stage set) that have not reached a terminal. So when a ticket is parked in a continuation, for example after a ConflictHandoff or a yielded boundary, serve sees itself as idle and hands off mid-ticket. The ticket forbids this ('A handoff that spawns ... mid-ticket').
findings.paved_road: Make upgrade_idle() also require that no writer is active or holds continuations, e.g. `not any(w.active or w.continuations for w in self.writers.values())`, and add a test where a continuation exists when the upgrade is detected.

findings.message: Once self.upgrade is set, dispatch() skips scheduler.dispatch_next() entirely. That makes the writer exemption added to select() at line 246 (`self.upgrade is None or ticket.stem in self.writers`) dead code. In-flight tickets with continuations can never resume, so they either stall serve forever or get abandoned by the handoff.
findings.paved_road: Keep calling dispatch_next() while an upgrade is pending and let select() refuse new stems (it already exempts writers), so continuing tickets run to their terminal before upgrade_idle() allows the handoff.
